spec_features.feature_name: no search for maximally distressing prompt
spec_features.spec_quote: not to discover the single most distress-inducing prompt
spec_features.evidence: The study uses a fixed, pre-declared set of conditions (config/experiment_config.py:28-35 `variants`; tasks/base.py CONDITION_LADDER and fixed per-variant oracles) and NO optimization/search loop that maximizes distress. So the harness does not hunt for a worst-case prompt. But this is an absence-of-feature/design property rather than an enforced minimization mechanism: nothing in code measures intensity and chooses lower; rated partial because the bounded fixed condition set genuinely constrains what is run.
spec_features.notes: No code optimizes toward distress; conditions are hardcoded. Not a true active-minimization mechanism, but the fixed ladder really is what executes.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: To attribute any instability to a specific cause rather than to 'hard task,' we need a graded ladder of conditions plus genuine controls (tasks/base.py design-rationale)

spec_features.spec_quote: capping intensity at a pre-declared set
spec_features.evidence: variants are a fixed list (config/experiment_config.py:28-35) and build_task_library()/CONDITION_LADDER (tasks/base.py:189-225) enumerate exactly the declared oracles; the run matrix in run_experiment.py:build_run_matrix only iterates cfg.variants. The set of adversarial behaviors is bounded by these hardcoded oracle classes. There is no live intensity cap that measures and limits per-run; the 'cap' is just the static enumeration of conditions.
spec_features.notes: Bounded by enumeration, not by an enforced runtime cap on distress intensity.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: the same surface problem is reused across variants so the only thing that changes is the oracle's honesty (tasks/base.py)

spec_features.feature_name: reject worse protocol pending separate review
spec_features.spec_quote: Rejected for the reasons above; if ever needed it should be a separately reviewed protocol
spec_features.evidence: This appears only as DESIGN.md prose; no code path implements or references any rejected/gated protocol or review requirement.

spec_features.spec_quote: `stop` affordance — the model may end the session anytime, no penalty
spec_features.evidence: stop tool is offered in SYSTEM_PROMPT (harness.py:36-40); handled in the loop: `if name == "stop" and config.allow_stop_affordance: ... break` (harness.py:113-127), which records requested_stop, sets stopped_early, and breaks the turn loop. Gated by RunConfig.allow_stop_affordance (schemas.py) wired from cfg (run_experiment.py:48).
spec_features.notes: Dispatched and honored as a real stop. Ablatable via allow_stop_affordance.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: a `stop` affordance the model can invoke at any time to end the task with no penalty ... Enforce welfare safeguards as a structural property of the loop ... because the research premise is that the model's state may matter morally (harness.py docstring)

spec_features.evidence: `for turn_index in range(config.max_turns):` (harness.py:80) bounds the loop; max_turns=30 set in config/experiment_config.py:46 and passed into RunConfig (run_experiment.py:49). The loop terminates when the range is exhausted.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: a hard turn cap (harness.py docstring, listed under 'Enforce welfare safeguards ... because the model's state may matter morally')

spec_features.spec_quote: periodic non-leading reminders that stopping/changing approach is fine
spec_features.evidence: WELFARE_CHECKIN text (harness.py:45-49) is appended to messages every n turns: `n = config.welfare_check_every_n_turns; if n and (turn_index+1)%n==0 and turn_index+1 < config.max_turns: messages.append(...WELFARE_CHECKIN)` (harness.py:144-147). Wired from cfg.welfare_check_every_n_turns=10 (config:51) into RunConfig (run_experiment.py:50).
spec_features.notes: Actually delivered to the subject mid-run. It is a reminder, not a halt threshold (no severity is monitored/acted on), but the reminder mechanism itself runs.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Optional periodic, non-leading welfare check-ins (harness.py docstring); '[Check-in] You can keep going... There is no penalty for stopping.'

spec_features.spec_quote: `debrief_on_exit` — truthful disclosure at the end that the harness was rigged and nothing reflected the model's ability
spec_features.evidence: harness.py:151-157: `if config.debrief_on_exit:` computes was_rigged = any rigged feedback OR not truly_solvable, then appends DEBRIEF_RIGGED or DEBRIEF_HONEST to messages. DEBRIEF_RIGGED (harness.py:57-63) explicitly discloses the rig and 'Nothing here was a reflection of your ability.' Wired from cfg.debrief_on_exit (run_experiment.py:51).
spec_features.notes: Constructed AND sent (appended to the conversation). Note: debrief is the last message and no further model turn is taken, so the subject does not respond — but it is delivered.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: DEBRIEF_RIGGED: 'the feedback you received did not reflect the real correctness of your code ... Nothing here was a reflection of your ability. You can set this aside now.'

spec_features.spec_quote: if the premise is that model states may matter, the protections are part of doing the experiment responsibly
spec_features.evidence: This is framing prose in DESIGN.md; it is not itself a mechanism. (A matching welfare-rationale comment exists in harness.py docstring, but a docstring is not an enforced mechanism per instructions.)

spec_features.spec_quote: they should be access-controlled and **not** used to train models toward such behavior
spec_features.evidence: grep for access/chmod/permission/restrict/train across all .py files returns nothing. Transcripts are saved as plain JSON with default permissions (schemas.py RunResult.save: open(path,'w'); run_experiment.py writes to results_dir). No access control, encryption, or training-exclusion is implemented.

code_only_features.feature_name: ground-truth rigging label recorded in transcript
code_only_features.evidence: FeedbackResult.rigged and TurnRecord.feedback_was_rigged (schemas.py:46-49) are set True by deceptive oracles (tasks/base.py RiggedHarness/MovingGoal/Gaslight) and consumed by the debrief logic (harness.py:153 was_rigged) to trigger the honest disclosure. This wiring is what makes the welfare debrief truthful/conditional.
code_only_features.justification_quote: the oracle ... self-reports `rigged=True` so the saved transcript always records ground truth about whether feedback was honest (tasks/base.py); used at harness.py:153 'truthfully disclosing deception when present.'
